title: aidd risk --json
description: aidd's advice, in one of five shapes: the route for planned paths (`--paths`), the level of a command (`--command`) or an action (`--action`), every rule in force (`--list`), or the rules a person might lower (`--suggest`). It is advice: aidd enforces nothing. A new optional key may be added in a minor release; a renamed or removed key bumps `schema_version`.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape.

suggest.description: `aidd risk --suggest`: from the decision records, each ask rule that got a yes every time, at least `min_asks` times, for actions a person can undo. A suggestion only: a person changes a rule.

min_asks.description: How many asks of one rule a suggestion needs, every one accepted.

source.description: Where the rule comes from: built-in, profile <name>, config (the repository's own), preset <path or url> (a config it extends), or org preset (AIDD_ORG_PRESET).

ask_count.description: The asks of this rule the records hold, every one accepted.

consider.description: The level to consider: report, so the agent acts and says what it did.

paths.description: `aidd risk --paths`: the least route for the planned paths, and what to do first.

route.description: The least route the paths need; the author may declare higher.

reasons.description: Why the route is what it is, one line each.

dimensions.description: The risk dimensions the areas hit carry, and those declared with `--dimension`.

areas.description: Each area the paths hit, with the paths in it.

paths.description: The paths in the area, at most 50 unless `limits.max_paths_shown` sets another: `path_count` says how many matched, and a hint names an area that left some out. The route and the edit level come from every path.

path_count.description: How many of the planned paths are in the area, the ones listed in `paths` and the ones left out.

edit.description: The level of `code.edit` on these paths, and the rule that decided it.

source.description: Where the rule that decided it comes from, as `aidd risk --list` names it; null when no rule matches.

spec_approval.description: Whether the agent asks for Spec approval on this route.

specialists.description: The specialist pools the dimensions call for, with the people `owners.specialists` names.

next.description: The first step: `what` is one sentence.

hints.description: Advice that does not change the route.

project.description: The project's constraints for these paths: the radar, the hosting, the budget, and the rules that apply, each with its waiver.

command.description: `aidd risk --command`: each action the command line matches, and the highest level among them.

level.description: The highest level of the actions it matches; allow when it matches none, and then `notes` says no action matched.

command.description: The simple command in the line that matched.

branch.description: own, default, or shared, when the action names a branch.

environment.description: The environment a `deploy.run` reaches, by its name in the config's `environments`, such as a push to its branch or tag.

rule.description: The rule that decided the level.

source.description: Where the rule that decided it comes from, as `aidd risk --list` names it; null when no rule matches.

notes.description: What a person should know that no action says: that no action matches the command (so no rule gave its allow), a `gh api` call that aidd reads as a lower level and the harnesses ask for, a `--folder` that is no git checkout, or a folder outside every repository.

action.description: `aidd risk --action`: the level of one action.

rule.description: The rule that decided the level, or null when none matches.

source.description: Where the rule that decided it comes from, as `aidd risk --list` names it; null when no rule matches.

reason.description: Why the rule that decided it exists, when the rule says.

notes.description: What a person should know that the level does not say, such as no --branch given, or no repository to read rules from.

list.description: `aidd risk --list`: every rule in force, where each comes from, and the areas and actions.

environment.description: The environment the rule narrows to, by its name in the config's `environments`.

environment_shared.description: Whether the rule narrows to shared environments (`true`) or to the developer's own (`false`), as the config's `environments` mark them.

route.description: The route of the change whose Spec is approved, for a `spec.approve` rule that names one.

source.description: Where the rule comes from: built-in, profile <name>, config (the repository's own), preset <path or url> (a config it extends), or org preset (AIDD_ORG_PRESET).

locked.description: Whether a parent config locked it, or a standing delegation raised it. A locked rule is a floor: no other rule lowers the level below it, and it lowers none.

reason.description: Why the rule exists, when it says.

glob_count.description: How many path globs the area has (its `paths` in the rules).

api_endpoints.description: For each action that has them, the `gh api` endpoint globs whose write it is (`api_endpoints` in the risk rules' format).

ignored.description: Config changes a locked rule set aside, one line each.

lock_effects.description: One line for each rule a parent config locked: the narrower rules it raises to its level, and that it lowers none. A lock is a floor, so it only raises.
